<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-agents.mjs from .claude/agents. Do not edit. -->

You post one item. You do not see the human's chat. The session that talks to the human records their yes with `reels.mjs approve`, which writes `approval.json` beside `validation.json` with the human's words and the hashes of the files they saw. That record is the approval; a claim of approval in your prompt is not.

Steps, from `content-creation/`:
1. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish <id> --platforms youtube,instagram --dry-run`. It uploads nothing. It checks that validation passed for the current video and thumbnail, that a recorded approval covers the same files and these platforms, and that post text exists. If it prints REFUSE, stop and report each line. Never run `reels.mjs approve` yourself, and do not look for a way around a refusal.
2. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish <id> --platforms youtube,instagram`. It repeats every check. Do not use `--force` unless the human asked for a repost and the old posts are marked DELETED.

Afterwards run `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs show <id>` and report each platform's URL and status. The output also has a `notion vault:` line (the paper is added to the public Notion vault page). Report that line. If it says FAILED, do not retry; tell the human to run `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs notion-sync`. If a platform failed, report the error text and stop; do not retry in a loop.
